scope: Actual bitnet raw-text multi-request product mode now uses the existing shared BnGenerateBatch scheduler and retained backend session pool, with layer-coordinated native expert-transfer reuse. One explicit native CUDA profile; this is progress toward the integrated four-profile CUDA release, not its acceptance.

interface.input: JSON array of1..64 nonempty UTF8 strings. File or -=stdin,16MiB serialized cap. Multiline/escaped text accepted; malformed UTF8/NUL strings rejected by bounded JSON document. No prompt IDs or continuations from reference files.
interface.options: --batch-live1..16 default2; --batch-token-budget default prefill_tokens*batch_live, at least batch_live and at most131072; batch per-request chunks at most8192; existing explicit RAM/GPU expert-cache, staging, maxseq and aggregate payload flags. Positive -n only; batch rejects --prepare-only and --token-ids because NDJSON already includes IDs. Single-request defaults/flags preserved. Current batch aggregate admission defaults and explicit-zero compatibility are documented in current_memory_evidence; the concurrency ceiling may exceed the enforced cap and execute with fewer live requests. --mixed-token-budget N optionally caps mixed steps; default0 keeps the full budget; positive values must be batch-live..batch-token-budget.
interface.output: NDJSON admitted/token/completed per implicit input-array request ID. Token contains greedy ID, output index and escaped counted UTF8 text. Completed flushes the independent decoder stream and reports generated count and committed position. Fatal execution reports failed for every pending ID when output remains writable; previously delivered prefixes remain valid. Broken output returns process1; it cannot deliver terminal events through a broken sink.
interface.semantics: Prediction-first length-bounded greedy generation: first token sampled from final prompt head, final predicted token not forwarded. Committed final position prompt_tokens+outputs-1. No automatic BOS/chat template/EOS stopping. Input file is a bounded static burst; common scheduler continuously refills available leases between steps, but no network server or persistent arrival/control transport added.
interface.trace: Optional --trace-dir existing directory: exclusive events.jsonl and request-ID-forward-N.i32le/.f32le files. No overwrite, trace IO error fails the batch. Trace mode is diagnostic and not valid performance evidence.

architecture.planner: Host aggregate bound expanded from8192 to16*8192=131072 to admit16 private2048-row requests. Per-request8192 cap unchanged; original134 independent captured schedules unchanged. New mixed16/32768 and131072 boundary units plus ASAN pass. CPU host planning does not declare backend packed-GPU limits.
architecture.preallocation: Every actual prompt and model/context limit validates before generated-output slab allocation; ASAN checks invalid INT_MAX output count rejects before GPU preparation.
architecture.scheduler: Existing public BnGenerateBatch: FIFO request-aware admission, chunk/token-budget planning, greedy finite checks, cohort-wide atomic sampling/publication, refill, cancellation between steps and fatal discard-all lifetime logic. No second model-family scheduler.
architecture.adapter: src/main_native_batch.h is main-owned backend adapter. Each request owns encoded-input/output slices and a streaming decoder state. Immutable encoder/decoder owners outlive all jobs. Pool owns backend request buffers/KV/history; GPU handles never attach to model weight structs. Model anatomy supplies vocabulary and shape; quant/model semantics unchanged.
architecture.execution: Uniform expert-placement policies partition each selected cohort. Multi-member partitions use native layer-coordinated shared expert leases and existing tiled GPU FFNs; singletons use existing full forward. Decode/small-row groups use existing individual FFNs, counted explicitly. Request attention, routes, activations, KV and history stay private. Full-tier widths/original folded B/M preserve source arithmetic; no concatenated-row GEMM.
architecture.backpressure: Each synchronous backend execute completes/fences a cohort, matching the common scheduler contract. Legal BUSY retries bind the same ordered native cohort, up to64 attempts. Excess backpressure cancels/discards every bound backend before generic terminal failure/refunds; no permanent spin. No bound cohort escapes between public scheduler steps.
architecture.failure: Trace IO or backend failure preserves previously published output prefix and discards all live execution leases; queued requests receive terminal failure. Output IO failure prevents further backend execution and returns nonzero. API/process restart required after fatal batch failure.

memory.managed: Common scheduler-owned HOST/DEVICE ledger now charges conservative shared payload plus live AND retained idle exact-shape native request payload. Request-sized max_tokens and rounded256-token capacity remain. Reserve before create/prepare; commit after success; fence/free before refund. BUSY preserves live sessions; idle storage may be evicted to fit a new shape.
memory.limits: HOST includes planned host and pinned payload and selected session/backend/arena C structs. JSON/index/setup peaks, opaque bookkeeping, allocator/driver/library internals, mappings and OS file cache remain outside the declared payload scope. Batch defaults16GiB HOST and90% free DEVICE; explicit0 disables that aggregate cap. Single defaults remain uncapped. Original numerical profiles and expert-cache policies remain unchanged.

bounds.scope: Actual batch product admits at rounded conservative planned aggregate caps; subtracting1MiB from either cap rejects after weight preparation and before request-pool allocation/any admission or output. Payload excludes documented metadata/driver/library overhead.

memory.telemetry: stderr reports shared/fallback cohort-layer steps, group/single counts, retry count, pool created/reused/evicted/discarded/restart failures and retained/peak request payload for all3 domains. Expert upload bytes/API time, RAM miss bytes, logical source-read bytes/API time are aggregate counters; they are not physical SSD bandwidth or exposed critical-path DMA stalls.
memory.historical_managed_scope: Retained idle AND live pool payload charged against device/host/pinned budgets. Request-sized max_tokens and rounded256-token required capacity; shared cache/model and pool accounting separate. Conservative full-ceiling*max_live pool budgets feed staged aggregate CLI cap checks; output slabs/input buffers and codec scratch included in planned host payload.

limitations: All four model families are not yet integrated into this common product mode; explicit capability matrix still needs a shared product-facing implementation.
This bounded static-burst CLI is not a persistent server with external arrivals/cancellation transport. Common library scheduling supports those controls but this frontend does not expose them yet.

No new matched vLLM performance or sustained throughput/TTFT/ITL-tail qualification; source tracing and stdout flushing affect timing. Previous static-cohort transfer speedup must not be attributed to this continuous-refill product schedule.
Cross-request kernels still use per-request GEMM launches; shared expert transfers do not concatenate activation rows into a single GEMM.

Per-request batch chunks remain capped at8192, aggregate host scheduling at131072; backends independently prepare or reject their GPU geometry.131072 is not a claim of a qualified packed-GPU row count.
No new ARM/Metal or other-model whole-runtime support claim; preserve original full goal.
